tex_content.html:
Proposition
[Equality of Mixed Partial Derivatives]

↗ def:partial-derivative ↗ def:multiindex-partial-derivative

\group Multiindex Calculus

For smooth $f : \R ^n \to \R $ and indices $i,j$, \[ \partial _{x_i}\partial _{x_j}f=\partial _{x_j}\partial _{x_i}f. \] Thus $D^\alpha f$ is independent of the order of the coordinate partials.
Proof

\sketch For a $C^2$ function,

\[ \partial _{x_i}\partial _{x_j}f(x)=D^2f(x)(e_i,e_j). \]

The Clairaut–Schwarz theorem makes $D^2f(x)$ symmetric, yielding the commutation identity. Any two orderings differ by adjacent transpositions, so the multiindex derivative is well defined.

□
